Try “A/B&nbsp;&nbsp;testing,” a feature that lets you&nbsp; choose up to 3 video titles and/or&nbsp;&nbsp; thumbnails to test with viewers to help&nbsp; pick your winner. Here’s how it works. Eligible creators can use the “A/B testing”&nbsp; feature through YouTube Studio desktop&nbsp;&nbsp; when publishing a new video, or with an&nbsp; existing video. On the Video Details page,&nbsp;&nbsp; click the icon under the ‘Title’ section&nbsp; or ‘Thumbnail section. From here,&nbsp;&nbsp; choose if you want to run a Title&nbsp; only test, a Thumbnail only test,&nbsp;&nbsp; or a Title and Thumbnail test. For title only, you can add up&nbsp;&nbsp; to three different titles to test.&nbsp; Titles must be under 100 characters.&nbsp; For thumbnail only, you can upload three&nbsp; different images to learn which viewers&nbsp;&nbsp; prefer. For title and thumbnail, you can add&nbsp; three different title and thumbnail combinations After you’ve added your titles, thumbnails or&nbsp; combinations of both, click Done. A/B testing is&nbsp;&nbsp; only available for Public, long form videos, and&nbsp; the test will start once you publish your video. Here’s how the test works:&nbsp; YouTube will show your chosen titles and/or&nbsp; thumbnails evenly across your video’s audience,&nbsp;&nbsp; and will select a winning thumbnail based on&nbsp; which one generates the most watch time share&nbsp; You can check the status of your test at&nbsp; any time by going to the Video Details&nbsp;&nbsp; page and clicking “View test report”&nbsp; under the Title or Thumbnail section&nbsp; You’ll see how much time is left for the&nbsp; test and how they’re performing. You can&nbsp;&nbsp; also choose to stop the test and manually&nbsp; set one of the options as the winner&nbsp; If you let the test run, the results&nbsp; may take a few hours or up to a couple&nbsp;&nbsp; of weeks to be finalized. How long it takes to get&nbsp;&nbsp; the results is affected by factors like: How similar your titles and/or thumbnails&nbsp;&nbsp; are (the more they differ, the&nbsp; faster your test will finish)&nbsp; And your video traffic (the more&nbsp; impressions that your video receives,&nbsp;&nbsp; the faster your test will finish) Once the test is finished,&nbsp;&nbsp; the test report will show the results If there’s a statistically significant result,&nbsp;&nbsp; you’ll see a “Winner” label. YouTube will&nbsp; automatically update your video title and/or&nbsp;&nbsp; thumbnail to this winner when the test is done. You might also see a “Performed Same” label.&nbsp;&nbsp; This result indicates that all test options had&nbsp; similar watch time performance. If there’s no&nbsp;&nbsp; clear winner, or if the options “Performed&nbsp; Same,” the first title and/or thumbnail&nbsp;&nbsp; will be selected and shown to your audience. Remember that in either case, it’s ultimately&nbsp;&nbsp; up to you – you can always manually select&nbsp; the video title and thumbnail you want to use.&nbsp; You can also choose to run a new test, but&nbsp; note it will delete your old experiment Now let’s walk through some things&nbsp; to note and best practices for&nbsp;&nbsp; using the “A/B testing” feature: Titles and Thumbnails must follow&nbsp;&nbsp; our Community Guidelines, and the tool will&nbsp; not work on videos that are designated as&nbsp;&nbsp; made for kids, for mature audiences, or live. Note that great titles and thumbnails serve&nbsp;&nbsp; an important purpose beyond getting viewers to&nbsp; click. They help a viewer understand what the&nbsp;&nbsp; video is about so that they don't waste&nbsp; their time clicking on the wrong videos.&nbsp; Remember that your title and thumbnail should&nbsp; work together as a team. We highly encourage&nbsp;&nbsp; testing title and thumbnail combinations&nbsp; to find which pairing works best to help&nbsp;&nbsp; viewers understand what your video is about. We suggest testing titles and thumbnails on&nbsp;&nbsp; a limited selection of older videos for&nbsp; initial guidance, then a selection of more&nbsp;&nbsp; recent videos you think will provide the most&nbsp; meaningful insights for your content strategy.&nbsp; We also recommend testing thumbnail&nbsp; variations that explore different&nbsp;&nbsp; layout compositions and changes to thumbnail&nbsp; elements (including background, text overlays, and&nbsp;&nbsp; object placement) to learn which resonates most&nbsp; with your audience. Some tips to keep in mind:&nbsp; Ensure your images are balanced, with a focal&nbsp; point to direct viewers attention towards&nbsp; Utilize high contrast, allowing&nbsp; your subject to stand out against&nbsp;&nbsp; the background in both light and dark mode. With text, remember that fewer words can be&nbsp;&nbsp; impactful, while too much text can be&nbsp; difficult to process while scrolling.&nbsp; And finally when it comes to depth of field, keep&nbsp; your background in mind and play with blank space We hope the A/B testing feature will help you&nbsp; gain insights when it comes to making titles&nbsp;&nbsp; and thumbnails, and help your overall video&nbsp; performance in the long run!
